author: val
body: This sits beside foreword-ranked-text-set rather than replacing it. That one pins the ordering semantics and is worth keeping for the CCE point it makes; this one pins the structure at production scale. The operand is the C# emitter's own keyword set, all seventy-seven, because that is the only payload the chapter carries in production and it is fifteen times the four-word set that was the whole of its coverage. Seventy-seven insertions reach a node height of seven, so levels zero through six are built and walked; four insertions reach height three and can say nothing about the rest.

author: val
body: Three independent readings, so a span defect cannot hide behind a walk that never touches one. ranked-text-to-list follows the level-zero chain and reads no span, so it can be believed while spans are in question and is the reference here. ranked-text-at and ranked-text-rank-of navigate by span at every level, so a span wrong at any height above zero puts them out of step with that reference. Membership descends the level ladder without spans and fails a third way. The absent, prefix-of-member and member-plus rows are the discriminating negatives: a lookup that answered True for everything would pass a members-only check.

author: val
body: The height a node is given depends on the count at the moment it is inserted, so a defect can be confined to one height and be invisible at every other size. This builds all seventy-seven prefixes and reports the first size at which a member cannot be found, rather than trusting one set to have exercised every level.

author: val
body: A nullary definition is re-evaluated at every mention, and for this chapter a mention rebuilds the whole set. Measured 2026-07-28 with a null control reading zero: ten lookups on a set bound once allocated 0 bytes, ten on a nullary-named set allocated 301280, which is 15064 per mention for a set of twenty-five. The plugs spell their keyword sets that way. CSharpEmitterExpressions names three of them in is-cs-keyword, so sanitizing one identifier can cost about 45 KB of permanent heap. The reading here is a boolean rather than a byte count so the row does not go red on an unrelated allocation change; the byte figures live in this note.

author: val
body: The two rows marked PINS A DEFECT pin the defect, not the behaviour. ranked-text-insert mutates the set it is given: after inserting fig into a three-element set the original handle reports size 3 while its own walk returns four entries including fig, so size and contents disagree and ranked-text-at on that handle returns a different value than before the call. Nothing is broken today because every caller uses the returned set, and ranked-text-clone exists because of this without saying so. The day those two rows change is the day the fix lands, and the red IS the fix rather than a regression to paper over. The real repair is either path-copying, which changes the cost model, or making the linear contract explicit; that is a decision, not a lane fix.
